name: World-integrated interface
summary: A world-integrated interface preserves presence when status and interaction surfaces inhabit the fiction while still meeting readability, input, interruption, and accessibility requirements.
player_action: The player checks status, inventory, equipment, objectives, or an environmental control without fully leaving the represented space.
system_response: The interface projects or embeds current authoritative state, preserves spatial context, and exposes equivalent readable alternatives where embodiment reduces usability.

conflicts_with: diegetic styling that makes essential text or state unreadable

failure_modes: World lighting or motion makes information unreadable.
The interface displays stale inventory or status.
Opening a surface silently pauses or fails to pause threats.
Style prevents scaling, narration, contrast, or alternative layout.
accessibility: Provide scalable, high-contrast, narrated, and screen-fixed alternatives.
State clearly whether gameplay continues while the interface is open.

smallest_playable_test.setup: Health, inventory, weapon selection, objective, and environmental switch interfaces tested in calm, movement, combat, darkness, occlusion, and accessible fallback modes.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: The interface preserves context and exposes current state without sacrificing supported readability or control.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: Embodiment works in calm scenes but fails under motion, lighting, or interruption.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: A conventional accessible alternative is required to understand state but is absent or semantically different.

evidence.claim: Dead Space UI lead Dino Ignacio describes holographic weapon, inventory, switch, screen, menu, and title interfaces built as gateways into the game world.
evidence.game_version: Dead Space franchise UI developer interview
evidence.notes: Supports world-integrated interface scope; accessibility requirements are bounded extensions to test.
